en.title: Rockstar Games Nearly Doubles Staff for GTA 6, Hires Real-World Experts
en.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 development saw Rockstar Games significantly expand its team, nearly doubling its headcount. The studio also brought in external professionals from fashion and racing to enhance the game's authenticity.
en.body:
Rockstar Games has dramatically scaled up its operations for the development of the highly anticipated **Grand Theft Auto 6**. Following the release of **Red Dead Redemption 2**, the studio nearly doubled its employee count, a significant investment aimed at bringing the next installment of the iconic franchise to life. A substantial portion of this expansion includes a dedicated new office in Los Angeles, which is reportedly focused almost exclusively on the game's non-player characters (NPCs).

This massive growth positions Rockstar at an estimated 4,000 employees, a stark contrast to its roughly 2,000 staff in 2018. The company has strategically expanded over the past decade, integrating new studios across Australia and India, alongside the new LA base. However, the expansion isn't solely confined to game developers. Rockstar has broadened its recruitment to include specialists from various industries to infuse **Grand Theft Auto 6** with unparalleled authenticity.

## Crafting Vice City's Identity

To capture the diverse and dynamic fashion landscape of **Vice City**, Rockstar enlisted the expertise of real-world professionals. Miami-based stylist **Jillian Carr** was brought on board to help construct a "fashion ecosystem" that reflects the varied styles, cultures, and social classes inhabitants of the game's world. Carr noted the city's emphasis on appearance, stating,

> "Vice City is built around vanity. Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly." 

Beyond fashion, the studio also hired professional racecar drivers to refine the driving mechanics and vehicle handling, ensuring a more realistic and engaging experience for players. Furthermore, 50 real street artists were commissioned to create authentic murals that will adorn the game's sprawling map, adding another layer of cultural depth and visual richness to **Vice City**.

## The Fan Impact

For dedicated **Grand Theft Auto** fans, these behind-the-scenes details paint a picture of a development process prioritizing immersion and authenticity above all else. The decision to hire external, seasoned professionals in fields like fashion and automotive design suggests a commitment to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in open-world gaming. This meticulous attention to detail, from character aesthetics to vehicle physics, is exactly what the community has come to expect from Rockstar, fueling excitement and anticipation for how these real-world influences will translate into the virtual streets of **Vice City**.

## What's Next

While **Rockstar Games** has not yet revealed a release date or further gameplay specifics beyond these development insights, the scale of their investment and the depth of their creative approach indicate that **Grand Theft Auto 6** is shaping up to be a monumental title. Fans are eagerly awaiting the next official update, which will likely offer more glimpses into the gameplay mechanics and the expansive world they will soon explore.

content_raw: Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more. As part of a cover story for Dazed , Rockstar Games shared a boatload of information about Grand Theft Auto 6. In the piece, it was confirmed that Rockstar doubled in size following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2 in order to bring GTA 6 to life, with a new Los Angeles-based office being "almost solely" dedicated to working on nothing but the game's NPCs. For context, Rockstar had around 2,000 employees in 2018. That would put them at around 4,000 now. The studio has expanded a lot over the last decade by acquiring new studios in Australia, India, and the aforementioned LA office. Rockstar's expansion doesn't exclusively encompass game developers. The company brought on other real-world professionals, such as Miami-based stylist Jillian Carr, who was hired to help create a “fashion ecosystem” that can capture the diversity in style, culture, and class necessary to give Vice City's people their distinct character. “Vice City is built around vanity,” Carr said to the magazine. “Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly.” Rockstar also hired racecar drivers to help with vehicle handling and 50 real street artists to design murals around the game's map. While consultants are hardly unique to this project, Carr and others are full-time employees at Rockstar and have been for years. Carr was specifically hired in 2023 and appears to be as much of the team's regular operations as anyone else. Rockstar also revealed new gameplay details for GTA 6 , such as how eating, working out, and sleeping all impact your characters and much, much more. It's just the start of a larger bombardment of GTA 6 information, too. Rockstar will officially pull the veil off the game tomorrow in an extended look on Netflix , which is widely expected to give us a deep dive on gameplay.
